headline: Bishkek sets 105bn som for schools; Talas has yet to see its own education chapter
dek: The Kyrgyz figure is about 10.1 billion Iradi som; the ISEZ spent roughly 4.2 billion on education in 2026, and the 2027 draft is due at the Mejlis this month.
paragraphs: Kyrgyzstan's draft budget for 2027 sets aside about 105 billion Kyrgyz som for education, most of it for pay. At the official cross rate of 9.6 Iradi som per 100 Kyrgyz som, that is about 10.1 billion Iradi som. The ISEZ's own education chapter for 2027 has not been published, and teachers here are waiting to see what it says.

The two figures are not like for like: Kyrgyzstan is a larger state with a larger school system. But the comparison is a useful one for the ISEZ, where the 2026 budget gave education about 12% of spending, roughly 4.2 billion of 34.9 billion som. Public wages as a whole took about 34%. IradOne reported the Kyrgyz figure on Wednesday, and the government said in a statement the same day that the ISEZ's draft proceeds to the Mejlis in the usual way.

The Ministry of Economy drafts the budget and the Governor's office sends it to the Mejlis in November. Deputies vote in December. Only a summary is published, so the education chapter may reach the public as a single line, or not at all. Asked whether the summary will break out education and teachers' pay, Bekbolot Sherov, the ministry's press secretary, said the draft would go to the Mejlis "in the usual way" and that pay "is set in som and paid in som". He gave no date for publication. Education Minister Kanykei Umotova's ministry referred questions on its chapter to the budget process.

The pay gap is documented. The Territorial Statistics Office puts the average teacher's pay at about 2,300 som a month, against an average wage of 3,250 som in 2025, so teachers earn about 71% of the average. About 1,400 teaching posts were vacant in 2025, worst for English and physics in the districts.

At the Bazar-i Kalan changers this morning the dollar sold for 11.90 som, against the official 8.40. At the street rate a teacher's 2,300 som buys about US$193; at the official rate it buys about US$274. "Our members are paid at 8.40 and pay rent and buy imports at the bazaar rate," said Rahat Osmon kyzy, chair of the Teachers' and Educators' Union, which has about 38,000 members. The union has asked since June for public pay to be indexed to the street rate, and no indexation has been announced. Ms Osmon kyzy said the union would judge the budget "by one line, not by the speeches".

In Nurzhan, Tatyana Voronina, who teaches physics at a city school, said her department has been short of a colleague since September and the two remaining teachers cover the extra classes. She said she knew of no one who had been told what next year's pay would be.

Prof. Raisa Akmatova, an economist at Talas State University, said the draft faces a choice it cannot avoid. Education spending is mostly wages, so any rise in the chapter is, in effect, a pay decision. "If the summary shows only a total, nobody can tell whether it is indexation, new posts or simply last year's pay at higher prices," she said. With consumer prices up 7.9% in September, she added, an unchanged chapter would be a cut in real terms.

The Herald made the same point in its leader on 14 November. The next fixed date is the Mejlis vote in December. What the summary says about the education chapter, and whether it names a pay figure, will be the first public sign of how the ministry treats the union's request.
